headline: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue rides off with the week's biggest poke
lede: Week 11 came in loud and left close, pardner. One wagon posted 126.0 and never looked back, while four other races were settled by less than 6 points apiece. With 2 weeks left in the regular season and 8 seats at the playoff table, every half point is silver in the pan.
paragraphs: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue hung 126.0 on Jrod and won by 38.38, the widest canyon of the week. Joe Burrow did the haulin' with 28.15, and the wagon still rolls at 9-2 with 9 straight wins, even with Mark Andrews turnin' in 1.5. Jrod managed 87.62 and left Ladd McConkey and his 15.85 sittin' in the shade, a lineup that a better hand would have improved by 15.1, droppin' the outfit to 4-7 and 2 straight losses.

Norskes U Betcha put up 111.57 behind Travis Kelce's 18.1 and finally broke through against Justin's Bad Team, 19.29 to the good. Justin's Bad Team got a whale of a day from Jonah Coleman at 31.85 and almost nothing elsewhere, with J.K. Dobbins returnin' 0.2 on the investment. That's 92.28 and a third straight loss at 5-6, while the Norskes climb to 4-7 and leave Tyler Shough's 16.34 unspent on the bench.

densmen rode C.J. Stroud's 23.63 to 98.88 and a second straight win, though the ledger still reads 3-8. Scott's Hype posted 81.02, the lowest score in the territory this week, and that's a 17.86 loss and 4 defeats in a row at 3-8. Justin Herbert did his part with 24.62, but the Vikings defense chipped in 2.0, and you cannot build a cabin out of kindlin'.

Warthogs leaned on the Bears defense for 29.0 and Jacob Rodriguez for 14.5, the best IDP day anywhere this week, and that was enough for 100.87 and an 8-3 record. Dart Star Orchestra answered with 86.96, George Pickens leadin' the way at 15.4, and fell by 13.91 to sit at 3-8. Courtland Sutton put a goose egg in the Warthogs lineup and they won anyway, which tells you how the day went for Dart Star Orchestra.

sisu squeaked past Zihuatanejo by 5.79, 100.2 to 94.41, with Ashton Jeanty luggin' the freight for 20.65. sisu left 12.72 on the table with a tidier lineup, Jacoby Brissett and his 16.27 watchin' from the rail, and still got there. Zihuatanejo got 25.11 from Cam Ward and a flat 0.0 from Dalton Kincaid, and now carries 5 straight losses at 3-8.

Aeil and Long Howie went to the last stretch of trail, with Aeil takin' it 119.23 to 115.28, a margin of 3.95. Jayden Daniels led Aeil with 17.53, which is a mighty tidy way to say nobody carried that wagon alone, and the outfit is 6-5 on 3 straight wins. Long Howie had the biggest gun in the game, Patrick Mahomes at 31.88, and nothin' to show for it but a first loss in a while at 8-3.

Dak Prescott went and struck the vein for 44.95, and HAWKSRULE needed every ounce of it to hold off Jack Attack 114.0 to 111.68. That's 5 wins in a row and a 7-4 ledger for HAWKSRULE. Jack Attack fell by 2.32 while leavin' 18.3 points of better lineup unclaimed, with Jacory Croskey-Merritt and his 13.25 parked on the bench, the sorriest set of lineup choices in the league this week.

The closest race in the territory: Super Troopers 101.1, e-mans revenge 100.19, decided by 0.91. Chuba Hubbard's 26.4 did the work for Super Troopers, who are 8-3 and winners of 4 straight even with Brock Bowers postin' 0.0. e-mans revenge got 26.0 from the Texans defense and takes a third straight loss at 5-6, though they do own this week's stat leader: Braelon Allen tops all 31 qualifyin' runners in Explosive Run Rate at 8% of carries.
sign_off: 2 weeks to go, 8 make the cut, and a few of you are 3 miles from the cabin eyein' a new valley. Set your lineups and ride.
purse: The commissioner's purse goes 4 deep this week: WeBleedOrangeAndBlue takes $40 on 126.0, Aeil takes $20 on 119.23, Long Howie takes $10 on 115.28, and HAWKSRULE scrapes in for $5 on 114.0. That's 8 weeks in the money now for WeBleedOrangeAndBlue, 4 for Long Howie, and 2 apiece for Aeil and HAWKSRULE.
